claim: qkv_gate's m <= 32 excess over the judge's speed-of-light (m=1 9.97 vs 8.42, m=16 11.36 vs 7.93) is geometry: r6 runs 144 one-tile CTAs on 132 SMs, so 12 SMs carry two tiles (max/mean 1.83). pw28 keeps r6's gv loop (12-bit dec1, register W ring, x in registers or through L1, escape walk, mma.sync with W as A) but cuts the 144 x 128 (tile, chunk) units into 128 equal CTA ranges of 144 units (9 warps x 16 or 18 warps x 8; max/mean 1.03; 4 SMs idle). A CTA runs its tile-B units first; at that switch step each warp stores its fp32 partial of a tile continued by the next CTA to its own workspace slot (st.relaxed.gpu, no fence, counter or barrier); the next CTA reads the slots at its end with ld.relaxed.gpu, re-reading while a word still holds the sentinel, restores the sentinel, and adds them in a fixed order (deterministic). In the interleaved order (V bit 4) the published part is finished early in time, so the end-of-kernel cost is one L2 read, not pw11's store-fence-atomic-load chain. 112 of 144 tiles have two contributors; slot traffic 0.5 MB (m<=8) to 2 MB (m=32), all L2.
paths: qkv_gate m=1/8: sk9i (9 warps x 16 units, interleaved, ST 2), sk9c (contiguous per warp, as r6), sk9i3 (ST 3), sk18i (18 warps x 8, 576 threads). m=16: sk9i (x in registers), sk9i-l1 / sk9c-l1 (x through L1, XS 2), sk18i-l1. m=32: sk9i-l1, sk9c-l1. Each validated with the template _validate (one-hot x8 bit-exact, random rows, odd m 5 / 9 / 17), declined if not all 128 CTAs are co-resident; PROBE skq times the best path and r6 alternately (3 x 21 replays, min) and the pick requires the PROBE min under r6's by MARGIN 0.99. r6, its 78 gv instances and the pw23 router paths are unchanged.
target_shapes: qkv_gate m=1: >= 0.8 us under r6 in the same bake (PROBE skq m=1 delta <= -0.80)
kill_if: qkv_gate m=1 best new path not >= 0.8 us under r6 in the same bake (PROBE skq qkv_gate m=1 delta > -0.80)
local_checks: nvcc 12.8 with the file's own flags (torch load_inline for sm_90: -gencode=arch=compute_90,code=sm_90 -O3 -lineinfo, --expt-relaxed-constexpr, -std=c++17): the 10 gvk instances have 0 spills (94-132 regs); SASS: 48 W LDG.NA per warp (16 x 3), 1 BAR.SYNC, no MEMBAR / ATOM, STG.E.128.STRONG.GPU only in the switch-step stores and the sentinel restore, one LDG.E.128.STRONG.GPU spin loop; the 86 pre-existing functions (r6's 78 gv instances + rr / rsk / rsk2) are SASS-identical to pw23. Two variants that spill (m=32 with x in registers, 192 B; m=32 at 18 warps ST 1, 24 B) are not built. proj_rsi/tools/gk_emu.py: coverage exactly once, producer slots == consumer slots, workspace all-sentinel after the launch, every tile emitted once, numbers at m = 1, 5, 7, 8, 9, 16, 17, 32 and one-hot exact, and the real _c12 pack + _gkesc escape lists (5223 escapes) restored bit-exactly by the kernel's walk, for all three unit orders; mutations (flipped list order, off-by-one slot predicate, dropped tile-B sum) fail it. A CPU mock of _gkbake builds every plan, dispatches through _gvcall and leaves the workspace all-sentinel. lint ok; cpu-check --official 9/9; 178 KB.
risks: The hypothesis itself: an SM with two r6 CTAs also has twice the loads in flight, so it may not take two tile-times; the PROBE m=1 line answers it.
Fewer W bytes in flight per SM than r6's two-CTA SMs at ST 2 (9 warps x 3 chunks, ~41 KB); sk9i3 and sk18i carry 1.33x / 2x.
Per-step unit address arithmetic and the switch-step branch add ~20 instructions per warp-chunk (issue is ~15% used at m=1 per the audit).

The consumer's spin relies on the producer (blockIdx - 1) being resident or dispatched first; all 128 CTAs are checked co-resident before a path is used, and the spin is bounded (2^20 reads: a broken plan gives NaN and fails validation instead of hanging).
